newsitem.title: USA: Record cold blankets central US, more cold is due.
newsitem.headline: Record cold blankets central US, more cold is due.

text.p: Frigid cold blanketed the U.S. midsection early Tuesday with freezing temperatures in Iowa and Nebraska shattering 80-year-old records.
The frigid weather may linger through May as a stubborn low pressure system over the Hudson Bay was forcing cold into the central U.S., meteorologists said.
Lows dipped to 28 degrees Fahrenheit in Sioux City, Iowa, shattering the previous 32-degree low set in 1910, said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.

Temperatures in Lincoln, Neb., fell to 27 degrees overnight and readings in Norfolk, Neb. fell to 26 degrees, shattering the 1914 record low of 28. Temperatures in Lincoln had never before been in the 20s this late in the spring.
"If there is any corn that planted early and emerged, it will burn it back at least," said Burgio.
The Midwest should remain cold through the week with another bout of freezing temperatures likely Thursday morning.
"Obviously it will keep development of the crop very slow for at least the next five days," Burgio said.

Weather Express Corp meteorologist Fred Gesser said the low pressure system over the Hudson Bay has not weakened as it normally does in the spring. This has kept cold weather in the central U.S., while a high pressure system over the Rocky Mountains has kept the West Coast hot.
June may warm up in the Midwest but Gesser said overall summer temperatures will average normal to below normal.
The combined effect of the Hudson Bay and West Coast weather system patterns may produce strong thunderstorms in the Midwest this summer.
"You are asking for trouble. It looks like a bumper crop of severe weather," said Gesser.
